chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the man who accuses his wife of adultery. He said: 'He is flogged, then they are separated, and he does not perform al-la'n (mutual cursing) with her until he says: I bear witness that I saw you doing such and such.'

key_terms.يُلاَعِنُهَا: he performs al-la'n (mutual cursing) with her

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for a husband accusing his wife of adultery without four witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural nuance in the *la'n* (mutual cursing) ritual, distinguishing it from the standard *hudud* penalty by requiring the husband to explicitly testify to personal witness (*mushahada*) before the formal cursing takes place. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise evidentiary standards within family law, ensuring that the severe spiritual consequence of *la'n* is applied only when the specific condition of direct observation is met, rather than merely for the accusation itself.
